basis: Cash net profit after tax from continuing operations, FY26 (year ended 30 June 2026) versus FY25 (year ended 30 June 2025). FY25 comparative information is restated to conform to the current-period presentation. The group total for FY25 cash NPAT from continuing operations ($10,252m) is unchanged from the value the bank reported in the FY25 Profit Announcement.

statutory_movement.note: Statutory NPAT from continuing operations, up 8%. Statutory NPAT including discontinued operations moved from $10,116m to $10,866m, up $750m or 7%. Cash NPAT including discontinued operations moved from $10,253m to $10,982m, up $729m or 7%.

cash_to_statutory_reconciliation.comment: Statutory NPAT grew $48m faster than cash NPAT on a continuing-operations basis because the after-tax drag from non-cash items fell from -$119m in FY25 to -$71m in FY26. The FY25 drag came mainly from losses on disposals (Bank of Hangzhou and other divestments); the FY26 drag came mainly from negative hedging and IFRS volatility. FY26 discontinued operations carried a -$45m non-cash loss for costs of the CFS disposal.

drivers.name: Net interest income
drivers.narrative: Net interest income rose 7% to $25,586m. Average interest earning assets rose $92bn or 8%, with average lending assets up $60bn or 7% across home, business and institutional lending. The net interest margin fell 3bpts to 2.05%; the bank states the margin was stable when it excludes liquid-asset growth. Margin parts: asset pricing -5bpts (home lending -4, business and institutional -1, from competition); portfolio mix +2bpts; capital, replicating and other +5bpts (replicating portfolio +4, capital hedges +1); Treasury and Markets -2bpts; liquids -2bpts; funding costs and basis risk flat.

drivers.name: Other operating income
drivers.narrative: Other operating income rose 4% to $4,638m. Commissions rose $135m on higher insurance income (this includes a milestone payment for the sale of CommInsure General Insurance) and higher equities income, partly offset by lower deposit, card and foreign exchange income. Other income rose $46m and includes a fair value gain on the Gemini investment after its IPO and lower Structured Asset Finance revenue after the aircraft lease portfolio sale. Lending fees rose $12m, funds management rose $12m, trading income fell $9m. The one-off gains (CommInsure milestone, Gemini) sit inside this driver and are not quantified separately.

drivers.name: Underlying operating expenses
drivers.narrative: Underlying operating expenses (which exclude restructuring and notable items) rose 6% to $13,585m. The bank's bridge: inflation +$455m, investment in technology +$444m, investment in frontline and operations +$128m, other +$96m, productivity -$404m. By category: staff +$288m (wage inflation, +1,760 average FTE), IT services +$393m (cloud, software licensing, amortisation, infrastructure/resilience/AI), other +$57m, occupancy -$19m. Favourable FX gave a partial offset; the bank does not quantify it.

drivers.name: Loan impairment expense
drivers.narrative: Loan impairment expense rose 9% to $788m (loan loss rate 8bpts, up 1bpt). Higher collective provisions reflect portfolio growth, increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty. By division: Retail Banking Services +$106m, New Zealand +$11m, Corporate Centre +$6m, offset by Business Banking -$45m (lower individually assessed charges and write-backs) and Institutional Banking and Markets -$16m. The divisional parts sum to the $62m increase.

drivers.name: Corporate tax expense
drivers.narrative: Corporate tax expense rose 5% to $4,699m on higher pre-tax profit. The effective tax rate (cash basis) fell 50bpts from 30.5% to 30.0%, primarily because non-deductible expenses fell. The lower rate softened the tax drag from profit growth.

notable_items.narrative: Restructuring and notable items within operating expenses rose from $130m in FY25 to $170m in FY26, a $40m extra drag on cash NPAT (pre-tax line). FY26 items: provisions for the settlement of legal proceedings in NZ (the Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act 2003 class action at ASB); an additional goodwill payment to certain customers after ASIC's Better Banking review; and domestic customer remediation. The bank does not split the $170m by item. FY25 items: domestic customer remediation $52m, NZ remediation $33m, Bankwest restructuring provision $45m.

disagreements.values: Profit Announcement (PDF p16, p34) says 9%; results presentation (PDF p24) says 8.5%.
disagreements.preferred: Both rest on the same dollar values ($788m vs $726m; +8.54%). The presentation shows one decimal; the Profit Announcement rounds to 9%. Use the dollar values.

disagreements.values: ASX announcement (PDF p1) headlines statutory NPAT of $10,911m, up 8% - a continuing-operations value. The Group Performance Summary (Profit Announcement PDF p16) shows total statutory NPAT of $10,866m, up 7%, after a $45m loss from discontinued operations (CFS disposal costs).
disagreements.preferred: Both are correct on their own basis. Use the continuing-operations pair ($10,133m to $10,911m) for comparison with cash NPAT, because cash NPAT is also headlined on a continuing-operations basis.

disagreements.values: FY25 Profit Announcement (PDF p16) originally reported FY25: Retail Banking Services $5,395m, Business Banking $4,092m, Institutional Banking and Markets $1,224m, New Zealand $1,198m, Corporate Centre and Other -$1,657m. FY26 Profit Announcement (PDF p16) restates FY25 to: $5,330m, $4,092m, $1,238m, $1,195m, -$1,603m.
disagreements.preferred: Use the FY26 restated comparatives for like-for-like divisional analysis. The FY26 document states comparatives were 'restated to conform with presentation in the current period'. The group total ($10,252m) is unchanged.
disagreements.materiality: Low - divisional re-allocation only; no group impact.

limitations: The bank does not split the $170m FY26 restructuring and notable items by component.
The one-off gains inside other operating income (CommInsure General Insurance milestone payment; Gemini IPO fair value gain) are identified but not quantified individually.
The favourable FX offset within operating expenses is not quantified.
Net interest margin drivers are disclosed in basis points, not dollars; the bank does not publish a dollar split of the $1,563m NII increase between volume and margin.
Analysis relies on text extraction from the PDFs; chart-only values were used only where the same numbers appear in tables or text.

All figures are on the bank's cash, continuing-operations basis with FY25 restated comparatives; expense driver signs are pre-tax line impacts, with the tax effect captured in the corporate tax expense driver.
